I stopped with `HAND-BACK`: the r188 scenario passes, but the r189 scenario can't go green until the spec has the r190 line the person asked for.

**Test run:** `python3 -m pytest -q --work-item w238` shows 181 passed and 1 failed.
- **r188** (the capability-proposal scenario) passes, from the earlier commit 440352d6.
- **r189** (the glossary-proposal scenario) fails. Its assertion `len(rounds(repo, "integrate", "g1")) == 1` fails because only an apply round for g1 starts.
- **Cause:** an apply round for a glossary-proposal that applied nothing has no route back to an integrate round. `supervise_glossary.ROUTES` says "no further round" (r167).

The person's answer was to add [r190] to the spec, but `spec/capabilities/supervision.md` still stops at r189. Spec lines and features are written by `formulating-features`, not by me. Building that route now would be code that no accepted scenario describes, so I changed nothing.

The next steps are: add r190, formulate its scenario, then build the route (`supervise_glossary.ROUTES` and `supervise_rounds.due`). After that, the r189 merge into g1 can go green.

`tools size` printed nothing, so no file is over 300 lines. This stage made no new commit. The plan contained no code. The report, with the starting suite record and open questions, is in `.shop/scratch/6-implement/report.md`.
